messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Error in unmarked occupancy model
parts:
Hi Angie,

A noticed a couple things. In your script you are assigning both the detection history (y) and the site-specific covariates (detectionhistory.site) to the same two columns of your input dataset (detectionhistory[,2:3]). Are these columns actually detection history or actually site covariates? They shouldn't be both.

If they are supposed to be the detection history (y), then you seem to have 2 observations at each site since there are 2 columns. Also I noticed that these columns have values greater than one (are they counts?). unmarked::occu() will automatically truncate any value over 1 to 1 so that the observations can be used in an occupancy modeling framework.

Assuming again that detectionhistory[,2:3] is supposed to be the observations y, when you supply observation-level time covariate, you need exactly 1 per observation. Since you have 28 sites (# of rows of y, or M) and 2 observations per site (# of columns of y, or obsNum) your time observation covariate should be of length 56 (28*2, M*obsNum). But in your code you generate a time covariate with length 84 (28*3) instead, which results in the error you saw. Maybe you want this instead:

time<-as.factor(rep(c(1,2),n))
detectionhistory.obs<-data.frame(time)

If I do this, and also remove the site covariate data for the reason stated above, I can get the model to run:

library(unmarked)
detectionhistory <- read.csv("detection_history_sample1.csv")
y<-detectionhistory[,2:3]
n<-nrow(detectionhistory)

time<-as.factor(rep(c(1,2),n))
detectionhistory.obs<-data.frame(time)
detectionhistory.occu<-unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, obsCovs = detectionhistory.obs)
(fit <- occu(~time~1, data=detectionhistory.occu))


However, you get a very large intercept estimate for occupancy because you don't have any sites where the species was never detected, again assuming columns 2 and 3 are supposed to be the detection history.

Ken
